correctness.rationale: Any length-three word has at most three distinct one-deletion outputs, giving ceil(q²/3) lower bound. The ten explicit optimal finite seed covers (q=2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,20,22) were fetched from the exact pinned data blob and independently enumerated, checking all q² ordered target pairs and codeword counts 2,6,12,22,34,48,66,86,134,162. For all remaining even q, published Colbourn–Hoffman–Rees 3-GDD existence (restated as Chang–Chee–Zhou Lemma 1.1) gives types 6^t u^1, t>=3, u=0,8,10. Insert local optimal 6,8,10 seed codes and two opposite words per transversal triple; every cross-group pair covered both directions. Formula sum ceil(g_i²/3)+2B=ceil(q²/3) with B=(q²−sum g_i²)/6 is exact, and these sizes exhaust all even q apart from the checked seeds. Finite checks are certificates for seeds, infinite existence comes from published theorem.

Xie–Sun–Ge 2026 Section V gives general q-ary deletion covering bounds and asymptotic construction but not the exact fixed-length-three all-even optimum. Group-divisible design existence is established, but combining it with directed-edge/triple deletion-ball certificates and finite sharp seeds is a nontrivial bridge. This completes a natural parity gap.
residual_risks: The same exact numerical value is published for odd q; the even parity extension should not be represented as whole-formula priority.
